coverage_note: Many Medi turns are English meta-talk (collocation drills). 09:52 English garble 'showed up as Shan Halloween' = probably أكلت شوربة; Amal said شربة شوربة then 'we can do both' - not a slip. 06:01 'في مدرسة' (another engine run wrote المدرسة) left out. 10:29-10:56 he asked how to say 'I was going to' - help, not a slip. 31:21-33:04 several '[foreign language]' gaps. Echo: 05:59 'um,' no Arabic; 06:33 'What happened?' = real English; 17:13 'في' = his answer. 1:01:07 عطلة - Amal later offered إجازة as a fit, not a correction. 'home' at 48:43 not on her sheet - not tier 3.

rows.why: He said 'throat hurts' with no owner ending; Amal prompted 'حلي... حل...' until he said حلقي (her chat 7al2i).
بوجع reads as 'I hurt'; the throat (it) needs بيوجع, as her chat beywajje3 shows; she voiced nothing (may be S4).

rows.amal_said: About. ... فيه، فيه الصبح. You need two فيهs.

rows.english: Do you know how to play this game?

rows.why: 'Listen to me' is a command; he gave present 'I hear you' and Amal said it's command, اسمعيني.

rows.why: Command to a girl; he gave the past 'you waited'; Amal gave ستني and explained -et is past, ستني is the command.
'Look at me' is اتطلع, not شاف; Amal said No, that's see me.

rows.amal_said: No. At me. ... At. تطلع علي.

rows.amal_said: No. Don't look. We're using تتطلع.

rows.amal_said: You said ما. ... But there's no ما. Why did you put ما؟
rows.why: He negated an affirmative sentence; Amal said there's no ما.

rows.amal_said: اشرحيني is like explain me. اشرحيني. So اشرحيلي is.
rows.why: 'Explain to me' needs -li (to me), not -ni (me); Amal said اشرحيني is 'explain me', it's اشرحيلي.
'Invite them' needs the object ending -hom; Amal said 'Invite them' and he said أعزمهم.

Same slip again after her fix; she prompted 'لا؟' (la-) and he said بنخطط لـ عرس (GR-32: wrong again after a fix is its own slip).
